Brought to you by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers. Start with a job, end with a career. IBEW Local 68. It's Leggy. Jeff, Jeff, Jeff. On Altitude Sports Radio 92.5. Let's go to the Ramos Law Hotline. Car accident, you need Ramos Law. Medical doctor and attorney, RamosLaw.com. Jeff Legwald joins the show. Hello, Leggy. Morning, fellas. You play your GTA yet today? You know, I've never played. How about that for an old guy statement? I'm shocked. It blows me away. Welcome to the club, Jeffrey. I'm no fun. Few of us left in this world. Leggy, as we get to the post-bye week, second half of the season, whatever you want to call it for the Denver Broncos, offensively, I just asked this to Chad Brown. I'm curious what your response is. How much can change from what we saw in the first half of the season to the second half just strictly on offense? Because nine games is a pretty large sample size and not making a move at the deadline. It's the same dudes. Can you see... a big step in improvement in the offense in the second half of the season, or are they just what they are? Well, I mean, there's both things can be true. I mean, they are, this is the group, you know, they have, but you know, they can do some things better technically, you know, they have, they haven't always been as smooth upfront, you know, blocking as they were last year with the same guys. I mean, last year they were, they were top three in run and pass protection metrics, you know, this year they're middle of the pack. So I think that is one area where you can fix some things, you know, better double teams, smoother, you know, chip and, you know, when the guard reaches and comes back and gets the guy on the other side, I mean, that, That can all be smoother. They can have better footwork. That stuff can improve. Running backs can be more decisive. I think Jonah Coleman is an example. He's a decisive runner. Look at the. Difference when he carries the ball right now than everybody else. He's the most decisive runner. So those things are fixable. You're not going to suddenly be faster, you know, quicker or any of those things. And they, you know, Bo can do a better job when he has opportunities. They're, they're terrible in, in big plays. I mean, they're down near the bottom of the. League and in plays of 20 yards or more. And in today's NFL, you know, the good teams can't be down there. You can't keep slugging out 10, 11, 12 play drives every week, you know, that kind of stuff. Can improve with the same cast. Jeff, yesterday Sean Payton was asked about any potential changes to the offensive line, and he shot that down in a hurry. He's not talking personnel. When will we know? Can you tell through practice? Well, I mean, you can hide it during practice. You can even hide it. I mean, often a team will line up in its real. Lineup during warm-ups before a game. You know, you can often track. Who's going to be where during a game? Who's in the nickel that day? Who's in the dime? What's the offensive line look like? They may not even line up how they're going to line up on the first snap in warm-ups Sunday. I think if he is going to make a move, it will be seen on the first snap of the game on offense. Jeff, I'm going to ask. I will add, Zach, he didn't exactly deny it. Let's just say that there's no denial in there. That's, that's a whole lot of. He was defiant in his no comment, put it that way. Well, you know, I, I, and I've, I've said this to him on other occasions, you know, he opened that can of worms himself. Nobody else did. He, he opened it on cow herd and he's mad that we're asking about it. You know, my, my theory has always been, You could talk to the local guys during the bye week and you wouldn't have this issue. But, you know, we move on. Jeff, I'm going to ask you to get in his head for a second here, please. He had four weeks with Davis Webb, five weeks under Sean Payton. If you had to ask him, hey, Sean, what's different now? You had basically two of the same sample sizes because we'll throw in the preseason under Davis Webb. What's different about your offense now that you're calling plays and he's not calling plays? What would the answer be, do you think? Because I don't see Jack squat. Well, he runs it more. He runs it a lot more. And the production may not be much different. But they've scored more points and they run it more. He is determined to settle down the looks Bo Nix is getting. from defenses so he can sift through them better. And he has done that by upping the carries in the run game. They've been far more, far closer to 50-50, 55, you. Know, 45. They've been much closer to. That run kind of, that kind of run-pass ratio with Sean calling plays. And he hinted at it when Davis was calling plays that, needed to be more efficient, needed to get more touches. So he has done that. Now, again, the run game production isn't much different, but Jonah Coleman was also hurt. For some of that. I will say. He's given them more carries, and their scoring is up. So I think he would put those two things together. Schedule also got a lot easier. It's getting a lot easier. Now with the injury– the Jets without Geno, the Patriots without Drake May, I mean, the back half of the schedule, if they're not in position to be arguing for the number one seed when Buffalo rolls in here, it'll be their own fault. I can't remember if I asked you this last weekend, so I apologize if I did, but I just watched Dion Henley lead the Chargers in tackling, and his knee looked fine. And we know the whole story behind this, but my overall question is, If the Broncos were in a position where they feel like they can get to a Super Bowl and he was somebody that could help them do that, and certainly they need a little bit of help from linebackers covering tight ends and running backs out of the backfield, he would have helped there. Why would they care if they're giving up the fifth or the seventh, even after that, if the goal is to win a Super Bowl and he can help now? I know there's long-term things that they think about, and I know that they value their draft picks, but a fifth and a seventh for some guy who could help you get to a Super Bowl, what's the point? Well, it was a fourth, was it not? I think they. Well, they would have still kept. Four and a five and a four and a seven. So it was a four and a five. So four and five or four and seven. It's really the difference between fifth and seventh, right? Well, I just. They valued that fourth-round pick. And, you know, again, every team's got its own medical framework. Their belief was. They saw imaging of his knee from last season and two seasons ago, as well as this season. And they didn't. Like what they saw as far as the progress of the condition of the knee. Now, he's been on the injury report for the Chargers this year as well. So they thought it was going to be an issue sooner rather than later. You know, if they turn out to be wrong, that's, you know. Does sooner mean this year? Well, I think they would have made the trade if they didn't believe that. I think their feeling was if they didn't get eight games out of them in the regular season and the playoff games out of them because of this condition, you can't control other injuries, you know, a guy rolling up on them and all that stuff. But I, I honestly, and I've been told they believed it would be an issue this year. And if they're going to, you know, if they're wrong, they're wrong. And they like the player. I mean, they, they could even pursue him in free agency next year if they, you know, they get the right price, but, I think their feeling was he wasn't the level of player where they would just say, okay, we're giving up the picks. No matter what. And, you know, I talked to personnel guys and I informally asked them and they were kind of split on it. You know, a few of them were like, he isn't the player where you're going to say, do the deal no matter what. And a few were like, okay, it's worth the risk. But, you know, they, I think the people have to remember, you know, If they're terrible next year, no one's going to be happy. None of, you know, nobody. And March is going to be a problem for them. They got a lot of guys up for free agency. They are an old team. They're one of the oldest teams in the league. And every pick is going to matter, including that fourth rounder. And they would have two in the fourth round now that they've kept it. So, I mean, that's why. They might be wrong. And it might be no issue, but they didn't think he was that level of player where you say do the deal no matter what. What is this mystery person, this mystery box, by the name of Caleb Lohner, who is now able to practice? You've talked about him. You mentioned him in the offseason. I've not seen him. What is this? Will he ever play? I hope so. Here's my theory, and it may just be too simplistic. It's the Timmy the Sportswriter theory. He's taller than everybody else, and he has a better vertical than anyone else on the field. And I watched this guy in an NCAA tournament basketball game throwing down dunks that were ridiculous. My theory is that Bo Nix simply throws the ball up really high where only he can get it, and they score touchdowns. That's what I want to see from Caleb Lohner, because I think he can do that. Will he ever play? Will he ever get on the field? He looked damn good yesterday. So, you know, color me hopeful. Oh, my good Lord almighty. Yeah, I'm not blaming you, Jeff, because I understand man crushes. You know, a guy gets hurt, he can't control it. But, you know, a phenomenal athlete. And I honestly, honestly, you know, all my years doing this, the injury thing is just, it's so brutal to watch sometimes how it's, Some guys can't get momentum because of it. The game is so unforgiving. And I don't think we give that enough credit sometimes. But I really hope he gets to play because he's a phenomenal athlete and he's worked his ass off. And, you know, just on a regular human being level, if a guy works his ass off that hard, he should get to play at some point in the league. Jeff Legwald joins us every single Thursday in all conversations brought to you by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, IBEW Local 68. Start with a job, end with a career. I just want to make sure I did. Am I missing something? A texter says Jeff does a great job as the color guy in college TV games. I'm willing to do it, but you know. nobody's been nuts enough to put me on live television for three hours. I was just going to say, I don't know if you did that or not. I want to make sure I didn't miss anything. Okay, so you weren't calling in. No, you didn't miss anything. No, you didn't. Somebody's got to. Ask me to do it first. No one's going to give this guy a headset for three hours live. Hey, Leggy, go ahead. You guys have it. Yeah, come on in, baby. You guys have it. You know, I can only think how many times you've been fined by the FCC for what I've done. Listen, man, I missed the first two hours of the show. I got to the house about 2.30 a.m. You could have just slid right on in at 7 o'clock. Get your butt out of bed, dude. Let's do the show. Either you're on the show or you're not. Exactly right. Yep. Can't make the club in the tub, baby. That's exactly right. Jeff, you're the best. Thank you. Thanks, fellas. I appreciate it.

title: Jeff Legwold Show on PHD 11-18-26
text: Hi, Jeff Legwald is joining us, brought to you by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, IBEW Local 68. You start with a job and end with a career. Scott, do you want to start with the question that you had going into the break, perhaps? Hey, Jeff, how are you doing? I'm good. How are you guys? Hey, we just discussed this. I had Darren give me his top five teams in the NFL right now, and as I can remember them, I think in no particular order. Cincinnati, Buffalo, Jacksonville, San Francisco, and Denver was top five. I said, well, give me your top five MVP candidates. Well, the top four, according to DraftKings or whatever the sporting book that Dan pulled up online, are Josh Allen, Lawrence, Burrow, and Purdy. And my question is this. Is there any– what's the correlation between having an MVP quarterback, having one of the best teams, and your chances of winning a Super Bowl? Well, they're always pretty high. I think in the Hall of Fame, I think Gibbs and Parcells are the only coaches in the Hall of Fame who didn't have a Hall of Fame quarterback. Wow. I think it's always been a pretty big correlation, and there's always going to be a year when– Maybe a defense is, you know, the Broncos, Super Bowl 50, when a defense gets you the trophy, but your most logical, consistent path is to have a real front-line quarterback, and then you're always in the mix. Because that player can lift a flawed team. I don't think anybody thinks the Cincinnati Bengals, top to bottom, depth chart, all of it, are, you know, one of the best put-together teams, but the trade that gave them Dexter Lawrence on defense fixed enough that if Burrow's going to play at this level, you know, yeah, they're going to be in the mix because, you know, Burrow's a guy who can just show up on a playoff day and have the day of his life and there's nothing you can do about it. Do you think the Broncos, as constituted, as they did not get anything out of the trade deadline, as it turns out, are constituted squarely enough to be legitimate Super Bowl contenders? And I will point out, on ESPN.com, your place of employment, they've got in a mock draft the Broncos drafting at 30. So at least whoever puts that together... thinks that highly of the Broncos. Do you Jeff think the same? Well, you know, I would, I say yes, because they've already beaten Jacksonville head to head. So, and you know, they've beaten the, the, the, you know, the Rams aren't at the front of the line right now, but they beat the Rams. They beat the Seahawks. They've beaten, they gave San Francisco, you know, until late. you know, they were right there in, in that one. So they've, they've slugged it out with some of the best teams in the league. And they played, I think now the math says they played the second toughest schedule through the first 10 weeks and they're seven and two. So you, you know, logically you have to say they're, they're good enough as constituted to, to get in the mix because they're already in the mix. And, you know, there isn't a too difficult of a scenario that they can end up with home field advantage. So then however it is, however good Bo Nix is, you just kind of say, okay, because the total package of the Broncos as constituted deserves that sort of recognition. I agree, by the way, I agree. The other thing in this mock draft that's kind of interesting, Jeff, is essentially saying this is it for Cortland Sutton and the Broncos will move on and get another big receiver and they have other ways to spend their money as well. Do you agree with that? Is this the last year for Cortland Sutton on the Broncos? You know, I can't say that yet. I don't know that both sides want that to happen, but that's certainly a scenario that can play out. I mean, they're, they're, they've already prepped in some ways. I mean, making the trade for Waddle is pretty much an indication. Somebody else is moving into the WR1 category when you trade a first-round pick for somebody. So I think they're moving toward that. I think they would love to have him around in their locker room with their players. And if he moves to a You know, as Rod Smith did late in his career. You know, Rod wasn't the primary options on a lot of plays, but he was good in the locker room. He was productive when he had the ball. I mean, if he's willing to do that as he gets older, I think he could stay here. But if he wants a more prominent role in those types of things moving forward, he may have to look elsewhere. A lot of rumors about possible changes coming out of this break and left guard. Your thoughts on that and what might be going on? Yeah, I mean, it's all on the table. He certainly, Sean Payton was not happy with the last couple weeks of offensive line play, especially against the Panthers. He thought and said in their meetings in-house that they thought they got pushed around too much against the Panthers. And, you know, I think most people have their, you know, even personnel people in the league kind of had their eye on Ben Powers' guard spot. there just because they've got the better options to make a change there if you want it. You're not going to move Bowles aside. You're not going to move Miner to the side. You're not going to move McGlinchey aside right now because you're not going to improve if you do that. The closest position battle in that group was that guard spot with Paul Chesky and and Powers, that was a close battle before any of this happened. So that's why everybody's got their eye on that spot because they have the best potential option there to make a change if they want to. We may not see it on the practice field. That may not be something you see until the first snap of Sunday's game. So you think Sean will keep that close to the vest today? Well, any day. I'm not even sure they would line up Usually the starters line up in warm-ups, how it's going to look in a game, and I bet they wouldn't even do that if they make a change. All right, well, fine. That's their prerogative. No problem. I got no abuse with that. I don't really want anything sneaking out. The Raiders coming in this weekend, brand-new quarterback, second start for the number one draft pick. What did you see from him last week, and what's the expectations? Well, he sure didn't get any favors. I mean, his first three starts will now be Seattle last week, Denver, and then Cleveland, who gets after the passer pretty well, too. So he got no favors, you know, from the schedule maker. You know, I saw what I saw of him coming out. Really, really quality processor. Really tough. You know, really... willing to hang in and make plays. And that sometimes can be to your detriment. You know, he took six sacks last week and, and got hit a few times that you don't want to see that. And they were even trying to, Clint was even trying to call a game to get the ball out of his hand quick. And I would expect that to continue this week, but he's really hampered. They can't run the ball at all. They're, they're last in pro carry. I think they've only had two games this year when a, when a running back is top 60 yards. So, you know, he's really hampered by what they have. And if Bowers is injury is going to be a problem, then they don't even have options for him in the pattern really. So it's going to be imperative for him to get the ball out of his hand, or he's going to, he's going to take a pound. Well, I was going to go there with you, Jeff is, is there inability to run the ball a results of, cause I think Gentian and Washington junior are both pretty good. And their offensive line does all right in protecting the quarterback and throwing the ball, at least with cousins they did. But they are one of the worst teams defensively. So I guess is there issues with the running game, the offensive line, running backs, that sort of thing? Or is it more a result of we're just losing or giving up all these points all the time or kind of chasing game after game after game? Probably a little of both, DMACC. You know, when you're chasing, you're never in good run situations. And I don't think they've been particularly good on first down. So, you know, you're second and eight, you're second and nine. That isn't real conducive to putting up quality run stats. But I think what happens is, you know, that group, the O-line and backs, don't have success early. The backs get kind of tentative because they're not, like, convinced the hole is going to be there. And in good run games with the best running backs, there's no hesitation. You know, they just go. And it may not even be... blocked up, you know, as they take the handoff, but they trust that the hole's going to be there. So there's a speed and explosiveness to the play. And that's what you really don't see with them. There's almost no urgency. explosiveness in the run game. The backs are kind of looking for an opening, and things are slow developing. And that's really shocking, frankly, for a Kubiak offense, because that's usually the one thing they can do no matter what. What are you hearing as far as Hufanga and Jones making their way back to the starting lineup? Yeah, I think, you know, I would certainly say Hufanga– I'd be surprised if he didn't play. I think he was close last week. I think Jones has got a good chance. But I think there's a shot they might have everybody back. Waddle and Moss are going to participate in practice this week. We'll see how that goes as they go through the protocol. I think they could have a chance to have most everybody back. The Raiders beat the Broncos like eight times in a row, relatively recently. Now the Broncos are on a four game heater against the Raiders. I would make the argument, Jeff, and I'm curious what you think until both of these teams are good at the same time. And there's something else between them. I don't know if this rivalry can spark back up like it, like it ever was. Well, the Kansas city one has, it's still there. Yeah. I mean, it's feels more like that. I just don't, where are you with the Broncos Raiders rivalry, Jeff? 4 0 Well, you know, it certainly doesn't have the same feel in the building. It was when Mike was here, Mike was here. He hated them. Oh my God. The Raiders were going to be a rival no matter what. And players knew it. You know, if you lost to the Raiders, you were practicing on Monday. You know, that was just, that was just a fact. And You know, I think once Mike wasn't here and then, you know, neither team could be good for an extended stretch. You know, I think that it lost some of the, the heat to it for sure. You know, I think, I think as you walk through the locker room these days, I think the chiefs are definitely perceived as the rival because they've got my homes and look, you know, no other team has won the division before. Since 2009 is the last time somebody else in Kansas City or Denver won the division. That's crazy. That's going to turn the rivalry to those two teams no matter what. I mean, that's a pretty long time for the Chargers and the Raiders to not be put together well enough to even win the division. Hey, did Mike ever get his money back from Al Davis? Oh, God, no. No, he always said no, so... I don't know that he would accept it now if the Raiders wanted him. That's a funny question. We've run into Mike. We've got to ask him that. Somebody wanted to give me $ 250, 000 that owed me from 15 years ago. I'm taking it. I used to tease Mike all the time with his business empire and all the money he made. He had two years where the Broncos and the Washington both paid him because he had no offset in his deal after he got fired here. I remember that. He got full salary from two teams for two years. That's awesome. And I said, after all that, you're still mad about that. He was definitely still mad. That's awesome. That's awesome. All right, Jeff. Good job. We appreciate it. And yeah, we'll see what happens here with Sean later today. I doubt he'll say anything, but wait, he does. We'll be here for it. My man, Jeff, we'll talk to you next week. All right. Take care, bro.
